notes.title: Hallusquatting — AI Hallucination Package Attacks
notes.summary:
**What:** Hallusquatting (Adversarial Hallucination Squatting) is a new supply-chain attack where hackers register package names that AI coding assistants commonly hallucinate, then embed malware in those packages.

**How it works:**
- AI coding assistants suggest non-existent package names when generating code
- Attackers pre-register these hallucinated package names on npm, PyPI, etc.
- When developers install the suggested packages, they unknowingly execute malicious code

**Key takeaways:**
- AI coding assistants hallucinate package names at a non-trivial rate, creating a new attack surface
- Attackers can claim these hallucinated names before developers use them
- Defense requires package name validation, lockfiles, and verified registries

→ This is an evolution of traditional typosquatting — AI hallucinations become a security vulnerability.

notes.title: Untracked — Optimize Docker Build Context by 99.8%
notes.summary:

**Key features:**

- Auto-generates `.dockerignore` rules
- Universal untracked file list for zip/lambda/webpack bundles
- Faster builds, smaller images, reduced bandwidth

→ Best for: teams with bloated build contexts looking for a quick win.

notes.summary:

notes.summary:

**Key techniques:**
- Generating background video assets using AI
- Frame interpolation for smooth scroll-based video playback
- Binding video progress to scroll position for interactive exploration
- Auto-play tour-based experiences for guided navigation
- Wrapping everything in KimmyK3's code generation

→ This workflow makes high-end interactive experiences accessible to non-specialists.

notes.title: Graphify — Turn Codebase into Queryable Knowledge Graph
notes.summary:
**What:** Graphify turns any codebase (with docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs) into a queryable knowledge graph using local deterministic AST parsing — no vector store needed.

**Key features:**
- Local deterministic AST parsing with tree-sitter
- Generates knowledge graphs with explained edges
- Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI
- Leiden community detection for clustering related code
- 99k+ stars — one of the most popular AI dev tools

→ This is essentially GraphRAG for code — deterministic, explainable, and runs locally.

notes.title: Wan2GP — Free AI Video Studio for Low-VRAM GPUs
notes.summary:
**What:** Wan2GP is a free, open-source AI video studio that runs on as little as 6GB VRAM, supporting multiple video generation models.

**Key features:**
- Runs on 6GB VRAM — works on RTX 10 series and laptops
- Built-in models: Wan 2.2, LTX-2, Hunyuan Video, Flux
- Text-to-video and image-to-video capabilities
- LoRA support for fine-tuned models
- Browser-based UI with queue system
- No upload, no watermark, completely local

→ The 6GB VRAM requirement makes this accessible to a much wider audience than most video AI tools.

notes.title: OpenWork — Open Source Claude Cowork Alternative
notes.summary:

- Reusable agent setups across organizations with guardrails

- Shared skills and MCPs across team workspaces
- Y Combinator backed

notes.title: CodeWiki by Google — AI-Generated Code Documentation
notes.summary:
**What:** CodeWiki by Google generates interactive documentation from GitHub repositories, including dependency graphs, module explanations, and beginner tutorials.

**Key features:**
- Paste a GitHub repo link — AI generates complete documentation
- Automatic dependency graphs showing code relationships
- Step-by-step module explanations

→ This eliminates the "where do I start?" problem for large codebases.

notes.summary:

**Key features:**
- One CLI for multiple social media platforms

→ This is the missing piece for agents that need to understand what's happening on social platforms.

notes.title: Microsoft TRELLIS.2 — Open Source 3D Model Generation
notes.summary:
**What:** Microsoft TRELLIS.2 is a state-of-the-art open-source 3D generation model (4B parameters) that converts any image into a production-ready 3D model in ~3 seconds with full PBR materials.

**Key features:**
- 4 billion parameter model for high-fidelity 3D generation
- Full PBR materials: base color, roughness, metallic, transparency
- Handles hair, fabric, glass, and complex geometries
- Outputs .glb format ready for Unity, Unreal, and Blender
- Runs locally, generates in ~3 seconds
- Full training codebase is open source

→ This is not a demo or research preview — it's a production-ready tool with full source code.

notes.title: AgentCookie — Browser Cookie Sync for AI Agents
notes.summary:
**What:** AgentCookie is an open-source tool that syncs browser cookies, CLI tokens, and API keys with AI agents using encrypted Tailscale connections.

**Key features:**
- Continuous laptop → agent sync of browser cookies
- Per-CLI secrets bus for bearer tokens and API keys
- Encrypted over Tailscale (AES-256-GCM)
- Works with Chrome, Stripe, Linear, Notion, Slack, and dozens more
- macOS only (both ends)

→ Solves the "my agent can't log into my services" problem securely.

notes.summary:

notes.summary:

notes.summary:

**Key features:**

- Vendor-neutral, open specification
- Designed for enterprise AI agent workflows
- Plain Markdown format for easy adoption
- Potential SEO ranking signal

→ This could become the standard for content verification in the AI era.

notes.title: Brinicle — Resource-Efficient C++ Vector Index Engine
notes.summary:
**What:** Brinicle is a resource-efficient C++ vector index engine designed for low-RAM production workloads, offering semantic search for text and images at high speed.

**Key features:**
- Runs on minimal RAM where larger alternatives like Qdrant crash
- High-speed semantic search for text and images
- C++ implementation for maximum performance
- HNSW-based indexing for efficient similarity search

→ When Qdrant or Milvus won't run on your hardware, Brinicle will.

notes.title: Ava-82M — Farsi TTS Model from Kokoro
notes.summary:
**What:** Ava-82M is a Farsi (Persian) text-to-speech model fine-tuned from Kokoro-82M, producing 24kHz single-speaker Persian speech with ~$0 budget training cost.

**Key features:**
- 82M parameters, under 400MB model size
- Trained on ~20 hours of Farsi data in 2 stages
- Total training cost: $0.90
- Includes Persian text frontend, number/date normalization
- CPU inference on Apple Silicon (~4.5s speech in ~0.9s)

→ Training a usable TTS model for under $1 makes this an incredible demonstration of accessible AI development.
